fees.asked: Why do I pay network fees in USDC on Arc, and roughly how much does a transfer cost?
fees.reply: Arc uses USDC for gas so you don’t need a separate gas token. A native USDC transfer costs roughly $0.00042 at the 20 gwei floor; typical transactions are around $0.001, though some materials quote about $0.01. Source: Arc gas and fees docs.

input.question: Why are network fees paid in USDC on Arc, and roughly how much does a transfer cost?

output.query: Why are network fees paid in USDC on Arc, and roughly how much does a transfer cost?

passages.text:
| Action | Gas | USDC cost |
|---|---|---|
| Native USDC send | 21,000 | 21,000 × 20e9 = 4.2e14 wei = $0.00042 |
| ERC-20 transfer (~40–65k) | ~50,000 | ~$0.001 |
| EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization | ~65,000 (docs) | ~$0.0013 |
| Contract deploy (1M gas) | 1,000,000 | $0.02 |

The hackathon slides quote "~$0.01 per transaction". The docs target ~$0.001. Both are negligible for agent use.

passages.text:
Kawase pays the network fee to set your wallet up and for payments inside your allowance. For payments you sign yourself,
a small USDC network fee is shown on the card. Bridges show the provider's fee before you confirm; swaps show the rate and
fees.
passages.title: FAQ: What does it cost?

passages.text:
Say or type who and how much — "send 20 dollars to Alex", "pay @mira 5 euros" — or use the Send screen. Kawase:

1. Finds the recipient: a saved contact, a Kawase @handle, or an 0x… address you typed yourself. The agent can only
   use an address that came from your contacts or appears word for word in your own message.
2. Picks the currency you hold, or asks if it is unclear.
3. Checks everything at once: your balance, your limits, whether this is a first payment to that address, whether the
   address looks like one of your contacts' (a look-alike), and whether a contact's address changed recently.
4. Shows the payment card with the exact amount, currency, recipient and network.

Then one of two things happens:

| Situation | What you do |
|---|---|
| USDC, inside what is left of today's allowance, to someone you have paid before or named in this request | Nothing. It is sent at once and Kawase says so. |
| Above the allowance, any EURC payment, a first payment to a new address above the threshold, or a look-alike address | Confirm with Face ID (fingerprint or screen lock on Android, an email code on the web). |

A payment is only marked paid when the network's receipt shows the exact transfer. If the answer is unclear, the card
says "still checking" and Kawase keeps looking; it never sends twice.

finality.asked: How fast is a payment final on Arc? Can it be reversed?
finality.reply: Arc payments reach deterministic finality in under a second, with blocks about every 0.48 seconds. They cannot be reversed on-chain once finalized; refunds require the recipient’s cooperation. Source: Arc overview and architecture.

passages.text: Arc is Circle's open, EVM-compatible Layer-1 "purpose-built for programmable money." USDC is the native gas token, so there is no volatile token. Finality is deterministic and sub-second: Malachite BFT under Proof-of-Authority, with blocks every ~0.48 s. Execution runs on Reth at the Osaka EVM baseline plus some Amsterdam features (EIP-7708). EURC and USYC are native at genesis. It integrates directly with Circle's platform: CCTP, Gateway, Wallets, App Kit, StableFX, and Agent Stack. Circle positions it for payments, lending, FX, treasury, and agentic commerce (arc-chain).
passages.title: Arc overview and architecture: One paragraph

passages.text:
- Move more than your allowance in a day, or use the allowance for anything other than a USDC transfer.
- Send to a recipient other than the one an automation's grant is pinned to.
- Swap, bridge, pay in EURC, pay a look-alike address or raise your limits without your Face ID.
- Approve a payment because of a spoken "yes": voice payments always wait for your tap.
- Invent an address: addresses come only from your contacts or from your own message, word for word.
- Choose the network: that is part of your session on the server, and every payment is checked against it.
- Mark something as paid without proof: only a receipt with the exact transfer counts. An unclear outcome is shown as
  "still checking" and never retried automatically, so nothing is paid twice.
